rationale_summary: The document primarily frames AI governance around protecting public health, safety, and fundamental rights from systemic risks posed by general-purpose AI models. The overarching objective explicitly references 'high level of protection of health, safety, and fundamental rights' and systemic risks defined as those with 'significant impact...on public health, safety, public security, fundamental rights, or the society as a whole.' Safety and security mitigations, systemic risk assessments, and mandatory reporting all center on preventing harms to users and society. Fundamental rights and social stability appear as strong secondary frames, with innovation enablement also present through the 'Principle of Innovation in AI Safety and Security.'

evidence_spans.quote: ensuring a high level of protection of health, safety, and fundamental rights enshrined in the Charter, including democracy, the rule of law, and environmental protection, against harmful effects of AI

systemic risk means a risk that is specific to the high-impact capabilities of general-purpose AI models, having a significant impact on the Union market due to their reach, or due to actual or reasonably foreseeable negative effects on public health, safety, public security, fundamental rights, or the society as a whole
risks of major accidents; risks to critical sectors or infrastructure, public mental health, freedom of expression and information, non-discrimination, privacy and the protection of personal data
Signatories will only proceed with the development, the making available on the market, and/or the use of the model, if the systemic risks stemming from the model are determined to be acceptable
this Chapter should encourage providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk to advance the state of the art in AI safety and security
